title: Short Stuff: Space Hurricanes
summary: Short Stuff episode on space hurricanes. Josh and Chuck explain the space plasma hurricane documented over the magnetic North Pole on August 20, 2014, reported in a Nature Communications paper in February 2021. They compare it to Earth hurricanes: it was about 600 miles wide, spun around a calm center at roughly 300 km/h (the transcript says "about d and sixty kilometers per hour," likely 360 km/h or similar), sits in the ionosphere rather than the 5 to 9 miles of Earth's atmosphere, and is made of plasma rather than water vapor and wind. They discuss the solar cycle and quiet space weather at the time, possible explanations such as magnetic field lines reconnecting, the satellite and GPS disruption risk, and the name choice over "space vortex." The episode closes with a teaser that a follow-up will come once more is understood.

segments.title: Introduction to space hurricanes
segments.summary: Josh introduces the August 20, 2014 space plasma hurricane over the magnetic North Pole, documented for the first time and written up in Nature Communications in February. He notes it was unseen at the time and compares its shape to Earth hurricanes.

segments.title: How space hurricanes differ from Earth hurricanes
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh explain that a space hurricane is made of plasma (ions, electrons, magnetism) rather than wind and water vapor, sits in the ionosphere rather than the lower few miles of the atmosphere, and was about 600 miles wide with a calm center. They mention a meteorologist who suggested the name space vortex.

segments.title: Space weather conditions and possible causes
segments.summary: The hosts describe the calm space weather at the time, despite the Sun being near its eleven-year cycle maximum, and say the event does not appear tied to the solar cycle. A possible explanation is magnetic field lines breaking and reconnecting, releasing energy. Scientists think these may be more common than realized.

segments.title: Impact on satellites and Earth
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck say the event is unlikely to affect people on Earth, though it could disrupt satellites and GPS and could be a concern for space exploration.

segments.title: Off-topic banter and sponsor read
segments.summary: Hosts banter about a seventies-style disco bar opening in Atlanta and goldfish, then give the show's iHeartRadio production credit and app promotion.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh wraps up, saying a follow-up on space hurricanes is planned once more is understood.
